NNA-499: Add corridor care checks to the ED site safety huddle every two hours, with the nurse in charge reading the corridor list and checking observation times.
NNA-500: Ask the healthcare assistant or triage nurse to ask older patients about frailty with a pocket Clinical Frailty Scale card at the first observations.
NNA-501: Ask the laboratory to phone high potassium results directly to the ED nurse in charge, who hands a hyperkalaemia treatment card to the treating doctor and checks calcium is given.
NNA-502: Stock a co-oximeter-enabled blood gas syringe and a suspected CO poisoning card at triage, with the triage nurse asking the exposure question and taking the sample.
NNA-503: Ask the ED pharmacist or nurse to check each anaphylaxis discharge against a discharge checklist, supply two auto-injectors from stock, and give the written plan.
NNA-504: Stock the standard renal colic analgesia pack in the triage room, and ask the triage nurse to start a pain timer on the observation chart.
NNA-505: Ask the nurse giving IV opioid to write the check time on the drug chart and set a bedside timer, with the nurse in charge reviewing outstanding checks each hour.
NNA-506: Hand each sepsis patient a safety-netting leaflet at the discharge desk, and ask the discharging nurse to record it on the observation chart.
NNA-507: Stock COPD oxygen alert cards at triage, and ask the triage nurse to give the card to the patient and prescribing doctor when COPD exacerbation is suspected.
NNA-508: Ask the ED nurse in charge to phone the early pregnancy assessment unit at the time of the positive test, and a named coordinator to review the list each morning.
NNA-509: Add an acute limb ischaemia phone script to the ED nurse in charge's referral card, so vascular on-call is called as soon as the diagnosis is suspected.
NNA-510: Ask the triage nurse to hand category 2 patients' notes to a named doctor, and put a visible timer on the ED board, checked by the nurse in charge.
NNA-511: Ask the ED pharmacist or senior nurse to review all new AF discharges each day, calculate and record the CHA2DS2-VASc score, and phone the GP if needed.
NNA-512: Give ambulance crews a self-harm non-conveyance checklist to complete with the patient, and require a call to the mental health crisis line before leaving the scene.
NNA-513: Add an indication check to the paramedic's decompression kit card, so the second crew member confirms instability and compromise aloud before the procedure begins.
NNA-514: Ask the ED radiographer or radiologist to phone any CT showing intracranial haemorrhage in a warfarin patient to the team leader, who checks PCC is requested.
NNA-515: Give ambulance control a STEMI destination card to read to the crew, naming the primary PCI centre and a call to the cath lab.
NNA-516: Give paramedics a laminated NICE traffic light card for children, and ask the clinical team leader to review red-feature non-conveyance cases within a week.
NNA-517: Ask the second crew member to check FAST and glucose values on a pocket card before handover, and the receiving nurse to confirm them in the pre-alert.
NNA-518: Add anticoagulant reversal to the trauma team leader's checklist at the primary survey, with a scribe recording haematology contact and agent decision.
NNA-519: Stock a severe pain pack at triage and ask the triage nurse to give the first analgesic and note the time on the observation chart.
NNA-520: Name a nurse in the ambulance queue area who checks observations on every waiting patient hourly, with crews asked to record the first set on arrival.
NNA-521: Ask the midwife in charge to call hourly fresh eyes checks aloud during the labour ward huddle, with a second midwife signing the CTG each hour.
NNA-522: Ask the midwife to set a bedside timer at each auscultation, with the coordinator reviewing a sample of partograms each shift for missed intervals.
NNA-523: Ask the midwife to move the bedside timer to a shorter interval when second stage is declared, and the labour coordinator to check this on rounds.
NNA-524: Ask the antenatal ward coordinator to confirm Bishop score and CTG at the induction safety check before the pessary or balloon is prepared.
NNA-525: Stock pre-filled oxytocin syringes with the correct dose in the delivery room, and ask the second midwife to check dose and route against the birth plan before giving.
NNA-526: Stock a PPH emergency box with a tranexamic acid ampoule and dose card, and ask the second midwife to call out the drug at the start of the response.
NNA-527: Ask the second midwife to be the timekeeper at every birth and call the cord clamping time aloud, writing it on the whiteboard and the record.
NNA-528: Ask the midwife to ask the mother's wishes at the antenatal appointment and record them, and the birth coordinator to check skin-to-skin at the handover.
NNA-529: Ask the community midwife to discuss vitamin K at the antenatal booking and note it in the hand-held record, and check the decision at the postnatal handover.
NNA-530: Stock co-amoxiclav in the labour ward theatre and delivery room stock, and add the antibiotic to the instrumental birth checklist read aloud by the midwife.
NNA-531: Name a postnatal ward coordinator to review the list of babies due a NIPE each morning, and assign each to a midwife or neonatal practitioner.
NNA-532: Ask the community midwife to complete the Whooley questions at each postnatal visit using a card, and the team leader to review a sample each month.
NNA-533: Ask the postnatal ward midwife to ask the mother and check the baby's chart at each shift handover, with the discharge nurse confirming before the baby leaves.
NNA-534: Ask the booking midwife to complete a VTE risk assessment card with the patient at the end of the appointment, and a coordinator to check it each week.
NNA-535: Stock a perineal repair pack with a pre-printed checklist sticker, and ask the second midwife to confirm rectal examination before the repair begins.
NNA-536: Add the episiotomy angle to the pre-instrumental birth checklist, so the obstetrician states the planned 60-degree angle and the midwife confirms before cutting.
NNA-537: Ask the maternity triage midwife to use a pocket reduced fetal movements card at the first assessment, and the coordinator to review any case seen without all three checks.
NNA-538: Ask the stop-smoking adviser to attend the antenatal clinic at set times, and a named maternity support worker to phone each referral within one working day.
NNA-539: Ask the booking midwife to complete the FGR risk assessment during the booking appointment, with the screening coordinator reviewing a weekly list of those still outstanding.
NNA-540: Ask the labour ward manager to hold a monthly training list reviewed at the team meeting, with a named midwife booking each person's session.
NNA-541: Give the diabetes antenatal clinic a named midwife who books each woman's 28-week HbA1c test and gives her a patient-held card showing the date.
NNA-542: Ask the neonatal nurse to prepare a pre-warmed delivery room checklist at pre-delivery, and a second nurse to record the first temperature with a probe thermometer.
NNA-543: Place a breast pump and kit in the labour room before delivery, and ask the neonatal nurse to help the mother express within hours of birth.
NNA-544: Stock PlGF test kits in the maternal day assessment unit and ask the midwife to run the test on first assessment using a pre-printed request sticker.
NNA-545: Ask the postnatal ward midwife to record a blood pressure reading before discharge and give the patient a written blood pressure plan and community review appointment.
NNA-546: Give the early pregnancy unit nurse a counselling script card listing expectant management first, and review a sample of consultations each month.
NNA-547: Ask a named early pregnancy nurse to phone each woman on day 4 and day 7 if the result is not seen, using a weekly methotrexate follow-up list.
